goal: mine spatial constructions so scene speech stops being telegraphic
result: FAILED. Of 820 located_in templates and 1026 part_of templates, the only ones surviving the quality guards (>=12 distinct argument pairs, not head-concentrated) are EMPTY juxtapositions: {o}  {s} and {s}  {o}. Adopting them would make speech worse, turning "Road in the near left." into "the near left road".
why: Two separate reasons, and the second is the deeper one. (1) In encyclopedic prose the arguments of located_in sit far apart with content between them, so the content-word guard rejects every real connective and only adjacency survives. (2) Wikipedia located_in is GEOGRAPHY -- Paris located_in France -- not scene layout. The relation name matches and the sense does not.
diagnosis: This corpus has no SCENE-DESCRIPTION REGISTER. That is the same wall this project already measured for fluency: the cause is register complexity, not corpus size. Encyclopedic text about entities cannot teach how to say what is in front of an eye.
what_would_work: a caption-register corpus (image captions describe layout in exactly this register)
or hand-authored spatial frames, which the realizer accepts as curated -- but that is AUTHORING, not mining, and would be a training wheel that must be labelled as one
not_done: No hand-written spatial templates were added. Writing them would have hidden this measurement behind a template, which is the pattern this project explicitly guards against.
